transcript.text: I'm in gas station brokerage. I'll do
about 2 million in revenue this year.
>> Amazing.
>> I'd love to get to eight.
>> Do you have a big team or it's just you?
>> Just me.
>> I'm going to take this to the
hypothetical extreme. The beauty of
your, you know, your role is that ticket
size will go up, right? Cuz your network
will develop and you'll get bigger and
bigger. You'll say no to smaller and
smaller deals. That is a path. It
probably takes realistically 10 years
for you to go from call it two to like
10 to maybe 15. If you want to scale
faster, you'll have to give up profit,
right?
>> You need to get more brokers or agents,
whatever, underneath of you who are
going to go sell. Think about this as a
cost of doing business in the business
that you're in. Is that like you're
going to have to take your foot off the
pedal by 20 or 30%? And the big unlock
for the business is that you'll have to
learn the recruiting, hiring, and
training process for brokers to onboard
them so that they are active. In the
deals that are too small for you, what
are you doing for those?
>> Nothing. [snorts] Maybe referring it to
someone.
>> Yeah, so I would use that as the bait.
>> Okay.
>> Which is like I'll give you all the
business that I don't want to do.
>> Yeah.
>> And we'll go 50/50 on it. And I think if
you do that, you're going to be able to
get a lot more interest. But the biggest
thing of all is just like it's an
expectation change. You want to make
more every year, and you can do that if
you don't bring anyone else on, but it's
not going to happen as fast as you want.
So you might have to take a step back.
>> Do you feel that's a path though? Like
should I like learn that?
>> 100%. If that if I mean,
I'm a big believer in don't change the
goal, change the path. Like I don't want
to negotiate on the goals.
